verdict.rationale: Glama's hosted MCP Inspector connects to any remote MCP server (Streamable HTTP/SSE, with OAuth/bearer auth) and runs its tools interactively, so the product does consume MCP servers. That use is manual testing, not an AI inside Glama calling the tools on the user's behalf. The Gateway and hosting proxy servers for external agents, and nothing shows Glama Chat consuming MCP tools. Missing for 10: evidence that Glama Chat or another Glama AI surface can attach MCP servers and call their tools agentically; persistent per-user server configuration in that surface; independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can plug MCP servers into this product so it can use their tools

citations.quote: Glama's hosted inspector connects to remote Streamable HTTP and SSE endpoints so you can inspect available capabilities and test requests interactively
Test any MCP server from your browser. Supports every Model Context Protocol feature, including tools, resources, prompts, tasks, elicitation, sampling, and OAuth 2.1.
Test your local MCP servers with the inspector by exposing them via a public tunnel using mcp-proxy.
